question:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the question that follows.

Passage:
Water is often described as the most precious natural resource, yet it is the one we waste most carelessly. India receives a large amount of rainfall every year, but most of it falls within a few months, and a great deal of this water flows into rivers and finally into the sea without being stored. As a result, many regions face acute shortages during the dry season, even though they received plenty of rain a few months earlier. Rainwater harvesting offers a simple and inexpensive solution to this problem. In this method, rainwater is collected from rooftops and open spaces and directed into tanks, ponds, or underground wells, where it can be used later or allowed to seep into the soil to recharge groundwater. Traditional communities in the arid parts of the country practised this art for centuries, building stepwells and small check dams that sustained entire villages. Modern cities, however, have covered the land with concrete, preventing rain from soaking into the ground. If citizens and governments act together to revive old practices and adopt new technology, the country can reduce its dependence on distant sources and protect its groundwater for future generations.

Question: According to the passage, why do many regions face acute water shortages in the dry season?

options.text: India receives very little rainfall every year
The rivers in the country have completely dried up
People refuse to use water from underground wells
Most of the rainwater is not stored and flows away into the sea

explanation: पैसेज के अनुसार अधिकांश वर्षा कुछ ही महीनों में होती है और उसका बहुत सा पानी बिना जमा हुए नदियों से होकर समुद्र में चला जाता है, इसलिए सूखे मौसम में भारी कमी हो जाती है।

question:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the question that follows.

Passage:
There was a time when a book was a person's constant companion on a train journey, in a waiting room, or during a quiet evening at home. Today, that place has been taken over by the smartphone, which offers endless entertainment in the form of short videos, messages, and games. Teachers and parents complain that children no longer have the patience to read even a few pages without checking their devices. Researchers believe that this decline in reading is not merely a change in taste but a loss with serious consequences. Reading a book demands sustained attention, and this effort strengthens the mind in the same way that exercise strengthens the body. It also widens vocabulary, sharpens imagination, and develops empathy by allowing readers to see the world through the eyes of others. Nevertheless, technology should not be treated as the enemy. Digital libraries have made thousands of books available to anyone with an internet connection. The real challenge is to use the device as a tool for learning rather than as a means of escape. Schools can help by setting aside a fixed time every day for silent reading, so that the habit of reading is not lost.

Question: According to the passage, what has taken the place of the book as a companion on journeys and in waiting rooms?

options.text: The television
The newspaper
The smartphone
The radio

explanation: पैसेज के अनुसार किताब की जगह अब स्मार्टफोन ने ले ली है (that place has been taken over by the smartphone)।

question:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the question that follows.

Passage:
Many people regard sleep as wasted time, an unfortunate interruption in a busy day that should be kept as short as possible. This belief is a dangerous myth. During sleep, the body repairs tissues, strengthens the immune system, and restores energy, while the brain sorts the information gathered during the day and stores important memories. Students who sleep adequately before an examination generally recall facts better than those who stay awake all night to study. Lack of sleep, on the other hand, affects mood, slows down decision-making, and increases the risk of accidents. Over a long period, it may also contribute to serious health problems such as heart disease and obesity. Doctors usually recommend that adults sleep for seven to eight hours every night, though the exact need varies from person to person. Experts also advise keeping a regular bedtime, avoiding heavy meals late at night, and switching off screens at least an hour before sleeping, since the light from them can disturb the body's natural clock. A good night's sleep is therefore not a luxury; it is a basic necessity for a healthy and productive life.

Question: What does the author call a 'dangerous myth'?

options.text: The belief that adults need seven to eight hours of sleep
The belief that sleep is wasted time
The belief that screens help people sleep better
The belief that students should study all night

explanation: पैसेज के शुरू में नींद को समय की बर्बादी मानने वाली धारणा के बाद कहा गया है: 'This belief is a dangerous myth.'

question:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the question that follows.

Passage:
Every year, millions of people leave villages and move to cities in search of better jobs, education, and healthcare. This steady flow of people, known as migration, has made cities the engines of economic growth, but it has also placed an enormous strain on them. Housing becomes expensive, forcing the poor to live in crowded settlements with little access to clean water or sanitation. Roads are choked with traffic, and the air is polluted by vehicles and factories. Meanwhile, villages lose their young and skilled workers, and agriculture is left in the hands of the elderly. Planners therefore argue that the solution lies not in stopping migration but in balancing development. If villages are provided with good schools, hospitals, roads, and opportunities for small industries, fewer people will feel compelled to leave their homes. Cities, in turn, can be planned better with public transport, affordable housing, and green spaces. Growth that benefits only a few places while neglecting the rest cannot be called true progress.

Question: According to the passage, why do millions of people move from villages to cities?

options.text: To escape the heavy traffic of villages
To find better jobs, education and healthcare
To start new farms in the cities
Because the government forces them to migrate

explanation: पैसेज की पहली पंक्ति के अनुसार लोग बेहतर नौकरी, शिक्षा और स्वास्थ्य सेवाओं की तलाश में गाँव छोड़कर शहर जाते हैं।

question:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the question that follows.

Passage:
Failure is perhaps the most misunderstood word in the language of success. Most people treat it as a final verdict on their ability, something to be ashamed of and hidden from others. In reality, failure is often the best teacher a person can have. A scientist may repeat an experiment hundreds of times before it succeeds, and each unsuccessful attempt reveals something that books could not teach. Students who fail an examination can, if they examine their mistakes honestly, discover weaknesses in their method of study and correct them before the next attempt. The people who eventually succeed are rarely those who never fell; they are those who refused to remain on the ground. Psychologists call this quality resilience, the capacity to recover quickly from difficulty. It cannot be bought or borrowed, but it can be developed through practice, support from family and friends, and a willingness to see setbacks as temporary. A society that punishes every mistake harshly creates cautious individuals who avoid risk and, therefore, also avoid discovery. One that treats mistakes as a part of learning produces creative and courageous citizens.

options.text: As the best teacher a person can have
As a temporary and harmless event
As a final judgement on their ability, something to be hidden
As a quality that can be bought or borrowed
